name: Xiang Hex
author: L. Lynn Smith (2008) / AGP port
description: The first hexagonal Chinese Chess: L. Lynn Smith's 2008 transplant of Xiangqi onto a 79-cell elongated hexagon (nine vertical files, the outer ones 7 cells and the centre 11). The seven-cell palace becomes a ring of hexes, the river becomes the board's horizontal mid-line of five cells, and every piece is re-cut for six directions - the Cannon still leaps a single screen, the Horse is still lamed by a piece on its leg, the Elephant still may not cross the river, and a Soldier that reaches the river gains two more forward directions and two sideways ones. Unusually, checkmate is only one way to win: a player who is stalemated, or who repeats a position, loses outright, and if neither side has a piece left that can cross the river the game is drawn.
